text: Alfred Carlton Gilbert (February 15, 1884 – January 24, 1961) was an American inventor, athlete, magician, toy maker, and businessman. As the founder of the A. C. Gilbert Company, he is known for inventing the Erector Set and American Flyer Trains. Born in Salem, Oregon, Gilbert attended the Tualatin Academy and Pacific University in Forest Grove, Oregon, where he was a member of the Gamma Sigma Fraternity. He left Pacific after 1902 and transferred to Yale University, financing his education through work as a magician and earning a degree in medicine. His thesis was titled The Genito-Urinary Phenomena of Athletes. An accomplished athlete, he broke the world record for consecutive chin-ups (39) in 1900 and the distance record for the running long dive in 1902. He invented the pole vault box and set two world records in the pole vault, including a record of 12′ 3″ (3.66 meters) at the Spring meet of the Irish American Athletic Club at Celtic Park, New York, in 1906. At the 1908 Summer Olympics, he tied for gold with Edward Cook, setting an Olympic record. Choosing not to pursue medicine, Gilbert founded Mysto Manufacturing in 1907 with his friend John Petrie, which later became the A. C. Gilbert Company. He developed the Erector Set in 1913, inspired by steel construction girders used on the New York, New Haven & Hartford Railroad; the set was preceded by Frank Hornby’s Meccano, which Hornby patented as "Mechanics Made Easy" in 1901. In 1918, during World War I, when the Council of National Defense considered banning toy production, Gilbert successfully argued against it, earning the nickname "The man who saved Christmas." He had previously contributed to the war effort by becoming one of the Four Minute Men who gave lectures to encourage war bond purchases. By 1935, the company had sold more than 30 million Erector Sets. He expanded the product line to include chemistry sets, microscope sets, and other educational toys, amassing over 150 patents over 50 years. In 1938, he acquired the rights to the American Flyer toy train line from W. O. Coleman and moved production from Chicago to New Haven. He adopted a 3/16 scale for the trains while retaining the three-rail O-gauge track associated with Lionel. After World War II, O-gauge track was replaced with two-rail S-gauge track. Gilbert was praised for his commitment to scale realism, making American Flyer trains appear more authentic. He is credited with originating employee benefits such as free medical and legal advice and maternity leave. In 1915, he founded the Toy Manufacturers of America trade association and served as its first president. Frustrated that invention was not taught in schools, in 1941 he opened the Gilbert Hall of Science in New York City, which promoted science interest and sold his products. In 1950–1951, he marketed the Gilbert U-238 Atomic Energy Laboratory, which included radioactive ore samples of autunite, carnotite, torbernite, and uraninite. In 1908, he married Mary Thompson, whom he met at Pacific University; they had three children: two girls and a boy. In the 1930s, they lived at Maraldene in Hamden, Connecticut, which included kennels where Gilbert bred German Shepherds, one of which won the Max von Stephanitz award. He also owned a 600-acre estate called Paradise, used for hunting and housing big-game trophies, and served as a venue for entertaining clients and guests at the Yale Bowl. Upon retiring in 1954, he transferred the company to his son. That same year, he published his autobiography, The Man Who Lives in Paradise. After his death in 1961, the family sold the remaining shares of the A. C. Gilbert Company to Jack Wrather, which went out of business in 1967, though the Erector trademark continued to be used. A museum in Salem, Oregon, named A. C. Gilbert's Discovery Village, honors him and includes historic structures such as the house of his uncle Andrew T. Gilbert, opening in 1989. The television movie The Man Who Saved Christmas, released on December 15, 2002, dramatizes Christmas during 1917–1918 in the context of World War I and features Jason Alexander as Gilbert; the film takes several historical liberties. Pacific University in Forest Grove, Oregon, opened a residential hall named after Gilbert in 2009.
